title: Shrink sliding window to seq_len//4
description: Changed short_window from long_window//2 to long_window//4 in _compute_window_sizes (train.py), at DEPTH=9/WINDOW_PATTERN=SSSS baseline: short-window layers now attend to 512 tokens instead of 1024, cutting attention FLOPs further and letting more steps/tokens fit in the fixed 5-min budget.
reflection: Adopted a1's proposal instead of my own duplicate-of-a0's DEPTH=10-under-SSSS idea, since running the same experiment twice would waste a shared slot. Result: val_bpb 0.993153 vs 0.998440 baseline, a 0.0053 improvement -- the largest single-round win since depth=9 (0.0037) and roughly 10x the SSSS pattern win it builds on. This confirms the 'cheaper attention -> more steps in fixed wall-clock -> lower loss' mechanism scales further than just pattern frequency; the window *size* itself is a real, strong lever. Worth pushing further next round (e.g. seq_len//8) and/or re-checking whether the forced full-context last layer is even needed once short windows are this cheap.
